claims.text: The proposed simulation explicitly incorporates defect structures into bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed simulation includes 1 wt.% oxygen.
Explicitly modeling defects and 1 wt.% oxygen will improve agreement with measured conductivity in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
Available high-temperature measurements were made on an analogous specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Oxygen may occupy substitutional or interstitial sites in HfNbTaTiZr.
Introduced defects and oxygen undergo segregation and develop spatial distributions in the alloy.
The modeled defects and oxygen distributions mediate phonon scattering.
The modeled defects and oxygen distributions affect charge-carrier mobility.
Defects and oxygen impurities create additional scattering centers.
Defects and oxygen impurities modify phonon dispersion.
Defects and oxygen impurities modify electron-transport properties.
Defects disrupt the idealized periodic potential assumed by defect-free models.
Defect-inclusive modeling will predict lower electrical conductivity than perfect-crystal modeling.
The conductivity reduction caused by defect-inclusive modeling will be especially pronounced at high temperatures.
Defect-inclusive modeling will produce a temperature dependence closer to experiment.
Perfect-crystal analytical models typically overestimate the electrical conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr from approximately 0 K through 1200 K, excluding the unspecified 200–300 K gap.
The approach is calibrated around material containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Validity depends on the assumed defect types and concentrations.
Substantially different oxygen contents or sample-preparation routes may fall outside the model's applicability.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and falsification design apply 1 wt.% oxygen across both temperature regimes, whereas the conditions field specifically associates the oxygen-bearing specimen with the 300–1200 K regime. It is therefore unclear whether the 0–200 K comparison should use an oxygen-bearing or oxygen-free sample.
